ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Viola Lee Blues jam and soaring New Potato Caboose
ai_show_review.blurb: The set features a blistering 20‑minute "Viola Lee Blues" that showcases Jerry’s incendiary leads, plus a rousing take on "New Potato Caboose" with strong vocal from Bob. All three soundboard sources capture the raw, high‑energy early‑Dead vibe.
ai_show_review.review: The Dead bring their A‑game to the O'Keefe Center on August 4, 1967, delivering a compact yet explosive two‑song set that epitomizes the band's pre‑psychedelic fire. "Viola Lee Blues" erupts into an almost twenty‑minute jam where Jerry Garcia’s smoking leads cut through the mix, while Phil Lesh provides a solid counterpoint that keeps the improvisation anchored. The follow‑up, "New Potato Caboose," is equally spirited, with Bob Weir’s vocal taking center stage and the rhythm section driving a tight, forward‑moving groove. All three soundboard recordings are clear enough to hear every nuance, though the Hanno capture (gd67-08-04.sbd.hanno.16752.sbeok.shnf) offers the best balance of clarity and completeness despite a touch of hiss.

best_recording.reason: Good clarity with balanced sound; captures the full Viola Lee Blues jam and New Potato Caboose with minimal hiss.

key_highlights: Extended, high‑energy "Viola Lee Blues" jam lasting nearly twenty minutes
"New Potato Caboose" delivered with soaring vocals and tight rhythm
Raw early‑Dead sound captured on three solid soundboard tapes
Jerry’s incendiary leads drive the improvisations throughout

band_performance.Jerry: Shows relentless creativity with smoking leads and a commanding solo on "Viola Lee Blues".
band_performance.Phil: Provides steady bass counterpoint that underpins the extended jam, keeping it grounded.
band_performance.Bob: Delivers a solid vocal performance on "New Potato Caboose", adding melodic weight.
